newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aerospatiale halts Dasa missiles, satellite talks.
newsitem.headline: Aerospatiale halts Dasa missiles, satellite talks.

text.p: French state-owned Aerospatiale has temporarily halted talks with Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa) over plans to merge their missiles and satellites activities, Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot said on Monday.

Michot told journalists the negotiations, dating back three years, were being "temporarily stopped" at their current stage. He blamed falling government orders for tactical missiles and uncertainties over German funding for its military satellite programme.
But the halt was not "definitive" and the companies are studying the bases on which to restart the discussions, he said.
Dasa is a unit of Daimler-Benz AG.
Aerospatiale has vainly tried to merge its missiles and satellite businesses into parallel joint ventures with Dasa but has been frustrated at the lack of a closure to the deals.

French conglomerate Lagardere Groupe has argued its Matra Marconi Space (MMS) joint venture with General Electric Company Plc (GEC) should be the natural centre for a European satellite business, and bring in Dasa.
Lagardere also wants its BAe Matra Dynamics venture with British Aerospace Plc to be the crucible for a pan-European missiles industry.

President Jacques Chirac agreed with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl at a bilateral summit last December that their governments would go ahead with the Helios 2 military spy satellite programme in two stages.
France would start work on the spacecraft this year but Germany would only join in 1998, as it lacked the seven billion marks needed for its share of the project.
